question: The sign of the magnification produced by a concave mirror is:

options.text: positive when the image is virtual and negative when the image is real
positive when the image is real and negative when the image is virtual

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sign of the magnification produced by a concave mirror is **positive when the image is virtual and negative when the image is real**.
 
• In a concave mirror, when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror, a virtual, erect, and magnified image is formed, resulting in a positive magnification.
 
• When the object is placed beyond the focal point, a real, inverted, and reduced or enlarged image is formed, resulting in a negative magnification.
 
• This property is a consequence of the mirror equation and the nature of image formation by concave mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnification (m)** is given by the ratio of the height of the image (hᵢ) to the height of the object (hₒ): m=hiho" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=hihom=hiho" id="MathJax-Element-71-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=hihom=hiho" id="MathJax-Element-21-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=hihom=hiho" id="MathJax-Element-15-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=hihom=hiho" id="MathJax-Element-9-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=hihom=hiho m=hiho m=hiho m=hiho m=hiho m=hiho m = \frac{h_i}{h_o} .
 
• For mirrors, magnification can also be expressed in terms of object distance (u) and image distance (v): m=−vu" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=−vum=−vu" id="MathJax-Element-72-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=−vum=−vu" id="MathJax-Element-22-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=−vum=−vu" id="MathJax-Element-16-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=−vum=−vu" id="MathJax-Element-10-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">m=−vum=−vu m=−vu m=−vu m=−vu m=−vu m=−vu m = -\frac{v}{u} .
 
• A **positive magnification** indicates that the image is erect and virtual.
 
• A **negative magnification** indicates that the image is inverted and real.
 
• Concave mirrors are used in various applications such as telescopes, shaving mirrors, and headlights due to their ability to form real and magnified images.
